lines.t: This skyscraper could fall over in a storm. And the only one who noticed was a student doing homework.
New York. Fifty-nine floors on four giant legs, because a tiny church refused to give up its corner.
The student calls the engineer's office. Your building is weak when the wind hits its corners.
The engineer checks his math. She's right.
And it gets worse. To save money, the builders bolted the joints instead of welding them.
If the power fails, a storm that could knock it over hits the city about every sixteen years.
So he makes a choice. Don't panic the city. Fix it. At night.
Every evening the office workers go home, and welders climb inside the walls. Sparks until sunrise.
By morning, the offices open like nothing happened.
Then the weather report. A hurricane is heading straight for New York.
The city secretly plans to evacuate ten blocks. Two thousand five hundred volunteers wait.
You see, the tower is like a table with wobbly legs. It's fine... until someone leans on the corner.
The welders keep going. The storm gets closer.
And then... the hurricane turns. Out to sea.
The repairs finish, and the secret stays secret for seventeen years.
Thousands of people worked in that tower every day... and never knew it almost fell on them.
Would you have told them? A, tell everyone. Or B, fix it in secret.
